From central forecourt they inspect surviving household ground-floor rooms x−30..40,y165..205, avoiding unstable collapsed upper floor and gatehouse interiors. Surviving roofed vestibule at west (~30x20ft), benches for public audiences, kitchen hearths, servants' common entrance and distinct domestic quarters show an actual functioning mixed household historically, not only a defensive stronghold. At northeast door-jamb the old-house mark and legible dedication identify apartment allocated to recognized child Valenthia. Mara compares with already copied D334 manor household register and copies the dedication/measurements; match is independent corroboration of household identity and a specific space historically assigned to Valenthia, not a recovered memory, birth date, proof he personally occupied it, parental fate or modern legal title. No verbatim invented dedication beyond supported content. Garden east x50..130,y110..175 surveyed, dry and overgrown, breach near(70,90) and ten-foot stone step with visible sound holds recognized as alternative return route around main gate; no climb or actual crossing yet. At record chamber x80..120,y185..215, observe east breach and unsupported cracked east-half floor before proceeding; Cirren/Fenar/Mara identify sound western5ft strip and north bedrock footing, party carefully uses only stable strip and footing to read both in-place docket tablets, avoids loading cracked section, no collapse, roll or loss. Mara and Cirren make faithful written copies/tracings of legible tablet contents: public audience arrangements, household allocations (including independent record of the same Valenthia apartment allocation), subsidiary Silverward service station, establishing concrete administrative relationship to seat. Copies retained by Mara, tablets remain in situ, no salvage claim or removal. Gatehouse exteriors inspected from stable forecourt, visibly unstable fallen roofs not entered, no accessible control instructions discovered in this survey, no guarantee none existed or reprogramming impossible; both Stone Defenders remain at original positions and unchanged. All accessible portions of prepared outer-seat scope surveyed, no further safe rooms established within current surviving footprint, no invented hidden dungeon or reward. Site identity established by matching cistern/aqueduct/twin gatehouses plus independent old-house marker/dedication, manor register and docket geography; local expedition's core historical discovery and copy evidence achieved, return route mapped but actual return not yet completed. Party returns to forecourt (0,135) around18:05, remains unarmed, exterior cache intact status not inspected/recovered; no further movement past arch, no extra consumption, damage, spells, feature spending, coin, title, appraisal or construction. Existing V purse, all character pools, rations/horse feed, D342 daily charge, LR1/6, Hessa/Voss/Flint Banner and other quest/custody unchanged. V next decision concerning weapon retrieval, camp, return or future plans; no unplayed actions assumed.
